title: Checks that keep infra safe
bridge: Infra checks are like ESLint and a type check for HCL: they run on every push and need no running system. Except the last step, a plan, needs read access to the real cloud. So CI gets a role that can read configuration and nothing else, and applying stays a person's job.
intro: Agents will soon propose infrastructure changes, and today infra CI only checks formatting. This lesson adds the checks that need no keys: tofu validate, tflint and trivy. Then it adds read-only plans on PRs with a role that cannot change or read data. Last come the walls that keep agents from ever applying.

picture.caption: Cheap keyless checks run on every push; a read-only plan is posted on the PR; a person applies.

sections.h: Start: what infra CI checks today
p: Today the infrastructure repo's CI is terrugrunt-lint.yml (the file name has that typo). It runs tofu fmt -check and terragrunt hcl format --check. Nothing checks types, insecure settings or the effect of a change. Plans are run by hand over VPN and pasted into PRs.
That was fine while only DevOps wrote infra. G7-17 adds checks that need no cloud keys, so they can run on every push, even on an agent's branch.
sections.because: We run the keyless checks first because they are cheap, safe on any branch, and catch most mistakes.

code.text:
# formatting only; exit code 3 and a file list when something is off
tofu fmt -check -recursive
terragrunt hcl format --check

notes.text: Formatting is checked, not meaning: a wrong type or an open port passes.
The same tofu fmt you ran in p4-1, for every .tf file.
The same for terragrunt.hcl files.

p: tofu validate checks types, references and required arguments, like tsc for HCL. With tofu init -backend=false it needs no state and no credentials, only the providers.
G7-17's new workflow, terraform-checks.yml, loops over modules/*/ and validates each one. It reports every failing module, not only the first. Terragrunt units are covered later by plans.
sections.because: We validate every module in a loop because one broken module should not hide another.

code.text:
jobs:
  validate:
    name: Validate modules
    runs-on: infrastructure-runner-set
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
      - name: Install Tofu
        env:
          TENV_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: tenv tofu install
      - name: tofu validate every module (no backend, no cloud keys)
        run: |
          status=0
          for dir in modules/*/; do
            (cd "$dir" && tofu init -backend=false -input=false -no-color >/dev/null && tofu validate -no-color) \
              || { echo "::error file=${dir}::tofu validate failed"; status=1; }
          done
          exit $status

notes.text: The repo's own runners, like its other workflows. Actions are pinned by SHA (p2-2).
tenv is a version manager for OpenTofu and Terraform, like nvm for Node. It installs the OpenTofu version the repo pins.
One subshell per module, so a cd never leaks into the next one.
::error file=...:: makes GitHub show the failure on the file in the PR.
Fail at the end if any module failed.

p: validate knows the provider's schema, not AWS's rules. tflint adds rulesets that do: the aws ruleset knows the real instance types, so a typo such as m8i.2xlage fails. The terraform ruleset flags unused variables and deprecated syntax.
G7-17 adds .tflint.hcl at the repo root with the aws and google rulesets, then runs tflint --init and tflint --recursive. GITHUB_TOKEN is passed so plugin downloads are not rate-limited.
sections.because: We lint with the provider rulesets because a wrong instance type passes validate and only fails at apply.

notes.text: Follow module calls inside the repo. Check the option's values in the tflint docs.
The recommended set: unused declarations, deprecated syntax, missing version pins.
Pin the ruleset version, like any dependency.

p: trivy config scans Terraform for misconfigurations. Examples are a bucket without a public access block, a security group open to the world, or encryption without our own key. Each finding has an ID, such as AWS-0107, and a severity.

G7-17 runs it over modules/, terraform/ and multi_tenant/ with --severity HIGH,CRITICAL. For two weeks it is advisory (exit code 0) while Security goes through the findings. Then new HIGH and CRITICAL findings fail the job. checkov is another scanner with the same purpose; the ticket picks trivy, and one is enough.
sections.because: We scan in CI because insecure settings look normal in a diff and a reviewer will miss one sooner or later.

notes.text: No public access block and no KMS key: four public-access findings and one encryption finding.
SSH open to the internet: the opposite of a sandbox security group (p3-2).
0.0.0.0/0 is the whole internet.

sections.see:
Failures: 6 (HIGH: 6, CRITICAL: 0)
AWS-0086 (HIGH): No public access block so not blocking public acls
AWS-0087 (HIGH): No public access block so not blocking public policies
AWS-0091 (HIGH): No public access block so not blocking public acls
AWS-0093 (HIGH): No public access block so not restricting public buckets
AWS-0107 (HIGH): Security group rule allows unrestricted ingress from any IP address.
AWS-0132 (HIGH): Bucket does not encrypt data with a customer managed key.

p: Some findings are accepted for a while. trivy reads .trivyignore from the working folder: one finding ID per line, with an optional expiry date. G7-17 asks for an owner and a reason on every line, and every ignored rule listed in the PR description.
An expiry turns 'accepted' into 'accepted until': on that date the finding fails again and someone must decide anew.
sections.because: We give every ignore an owner and a date because unowned exceptions become permanent holes.

code.text:
# owner=devops reason=G3-04 adds the bucket's own KMS key in the next PR
AWS-0132 exp:2026-12-31
# every entry: who owns it, why it is acceptable, and until when (G7-17)

notes.text: A comment line: who owns this exception and why it is acceptable now.
The finding ID, and the date after which trivy reports it again.
Security reviews this file; agents may not change it (section 7).

p: A plan needs to read the real account. G7-30 adds TerraformPlanRole to each account: ReadOnlyAccess plus an explicit Deny on data reads (s3:GetObject, secrets, parameters, kms:Decrypt). An OIDC role in inf, GitHubActionsTerraformPlan, may assume it; it trusts only repo:RhinoHealth/infrastructure:pull_request.

G7-32's workflow plans the units a PR changes, as that role. account.hcl reads the role name from TG_ROLE_NAME. The role can write nothing, so plans run with -lock=false. Plans never use -out, because a plan file holds secret values in plain text. One sticky comment per PR shows each unit's summary line.
sections.because: We plan with a role that cannot write because then a malicious PR can at worst read configuration, never change the cloud.

code.text:
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['terraform/**', 'modules/**', 'multi_tenant/**', 'single_tenant/**']

permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read, pull-requests: write }

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: infrastructure-runner-set
    env:
      TG_ROLE_NAME: TerraformPlanRole  # read by account.hcl (G7-30); never TerraformDeploymentRole here
    steps:
      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@<sha> # pin by SHA
        with: { aws-region: us-east-1, role-to-assume: "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActionsTerraformPlan" }
      - name: Plan the changed units (read-only, no lock, no plan files)
        run: |
          git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep 'terragrunt.hcl$' | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u > units.txt
          while read -r unit; do
            (cd "$unit" && terragrunt plan -lock=false -input=false -no-color) > "plan-${unit//\//_}.txt" 2>&1 || true
          done < units.txt
      - name: One comment with the summary per unit
        env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}" }
        run: .github/scripts/post_plan_comment.sh units.txt

notes.text: id-token: write lets the job get an OIDC token (p2-3). No stored AWS keys.
account.hcl builds the role ARN from this, so every unit assumes the plan role.
The OIDC role in inf; it trusts pull_request runs of this repo only (G7-30).
Units are folders with a changed terragrunt.hcl. Module-only changes need Terragrunt's 'units reading' option.
-lock=false because the role cannot write a lock; no -out because plan files hold secrets.

p: An agent may write HCL, run fmt, validate, tflint and trivy, and read the plan comment. It never runs apply, destroy, sync or workflow_dispatch. Nothing in these workflows can apply, and agents hold no role that could.

Agents also never change the checks they are judged by. G7-17 asks for terraform-checks.yml, .tflint.hcl and .trivyignore to be on the protected paths agents may not edit (G0, G3). G0 must first narrow Vault's gha-runners role and add a read-only Vault role. Until then, PR plans skip the units that need Vault or EKS, our Kubernetes clusters.

callout.text: Agents never merge, apply, destroy, sync or dispatch, and never edit the checks that judge them. A plan in a comment is information; applying it is a person's decision.

quiz.q: Why can tofu validate run on every push, even on an agent's branch?

options.text: It runs with -backend=false: no state, no credentials, only the providers
options.why: Nothing secret is needed, so nothing secret can leak.

options.text: Because GitHub hides the AWS keys from forks
options.why: validate uses no AWS keys at all.
fmt checks formatting; validate checks types, references and required arguments.

quiz.q: Why do PR plans run with -lock=false and never with -out?

options.text: Locks and plan files are not supported by Terragrunt
options.why: Both are supported; we choose not to use them.

options.text: The plan role cannot write a lock, and a plan file holds secret values in plain text
options.why: A read-only role cannot write, and an artifact with secrets must not exist.

quiz.q: An agent's PR adds a line to .trivyignore so its change passes. What should happen?

options.why: It is one of the checks the agent is judged by.

options.text: The change is blocked: .trivyignore is a protected path agents may not edit
options.why: Agents never change the checks they are judged by.

options.text: trivy ignores entries written by bots
options.why: trivy cannot tell who wrote a line; the protection is on the path.

words.plain: Checks types, references and required arguments with no state or credentials.
A linter for HCL with provider rulesets that know real values such as instance types.
A scanner for insecure settings in Terraform, with finding IDs and severities.
The list of accepted findings, one ID per line, each with an owner, a reason and an expiry.
A per-account role with read access to configuration and a Deny on data reads.
One PR comment that the workflow updates on each push instead of adding new ones.
A file agents may not change, such as the checks that judge them.

tickets.why: Adds tofu validate, tflint and trivy config to infrastructure CI, with no cloud keys.
The read-only TerraformPlanRole per account and the OIDC role that only PR runs may assume.
Posts read-only Terragrunt plans on infrastructure PRs; nothing in it can apply.

remember: Keyless checks on every push, a read-only plan on every PR, and a person applies. Agents never touch the checks or the apply.
